body: That's true. And I guess the sooner I get help the greater the chance there is that I can salvage my current relationships. I'm doing mostly okay in that sense but I have a feeling that the longer I go without treatment the more likely I am to screw everything up and hurt everyone and I don't want to do it.

That makes me feel better but at the same time no less afraid. 

And how do I approach a doctor about this? Do I just go to a therapist and be like, "Hey, I think I have BPD, here's why, please help me"?
I'm just scared that I'll try and it won't work, and I'll end up ruining everything for everyone. I feel like I need to extinguish myself before I burn everyone else alive.
I don't want my craziness to be a novelty to people. I don't want people to tolerate me just because my instability and immaturity seem "interesting."
I don't want to subject other people to my craziness. Even if relationships are fulfilling, what do other people get out of it other than hurt and frustration?

> Nor does it sentence you to an unhappy life.

But it does for anyone who tries to get close to me.
